en.title: Colliding Object Pairs Within Chebyshev Distance
en.description:
Given the integer center coordinates of n objects. By the criterion stated explicitly in the original problem, two different objects collide if and only if |x₁−x₂|≤1 and |y₁−y₂|≤1. Find the number of unordered colliding pairs; different objects at the same coordinates also form a pair. This distance criterion takes precedence; do not derive it from the side lengths in the figure.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..1000), followed by n lines of x y (−10000..10000).
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: (1,1) and each of the other three objects have both coordinate differences at most 1, and no other pair qualifies, so there are 3 pairs in total.
hints: Read the coordinates one by one, look up and add the number of objects already at the nine neighboring integer coordinates, then record the current object.
